doc.title: Frank Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 7, 1998

chapter: Joining and playing in the Basie band
title: Back in Detroit and hired by Count Basie
summary: Back in uniform in May 1953 he learned Basie was looking for him and joined the band on July 27, 1953.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: And after being released and shipped back to the United States, I came back to Detroit, now this was May of 1953. My first day in town, I don’t have any civilian clothes, I’m walking around in my Army uniform, I ran into an old friend who said, “Count Basie is looking for you.” I said, “Count Basie’s looking for me? Nobody knows I’m here.” He said, “Count Basie’s looking for you, you’d better go over to the—” I forget what the ballroom, the Graystone Ballroom or something like that. The Basie band was actually appearing that night. So I went over there and surely enough, Lockjaw Davis was planning to leave and Ernie Wilkins and Jimmy Wilkins, who were in the band at the time, Jimmy with whom I’d been in college, Jimmy Wilkins had been my band leader in Wilberforce University, the leader of the Wilberforce Collegians. And they, along with Billy Eckstine had recommended me for the band but they didn’t know where I was at the time. So I showed up.
The right place at the right time and three months later I was in the Count Basie Orchestra, July 27, 1953.
Had you had a chance while you were in the service to still be listening to recordings of them?
Not too much. I was listening to a lot of small groups at the time. There weren’t too many things happening.
Well plus he had broken up the band for a short time.
He had broken up the band from 1949 to about ‘52 I think.
So you kind of got in on the New Testament band.
That’s right, at pretty much the beginning of the New Testament band.
Right. That’s really, I’m sure it makes great print in your book.
My first day back and I’m still walking around in my uniform.
That’s right. It’s a true story. And I mean I couldn’t have made that up.
There are other stories in there that I could never have made up either.
